original_question: Consider a 4-manifold endowed with a foliation F by surfaces. Can the foliation be perturbed to an Engel structure?
target_in_paper: Question 2.16 in §2.5 (Engel structures): "Consider a 4-manifold endowed with a foliation F by surfaces. Can the foliation be perturbed to an Engel structure?" The draft is essentially targeting this question verbatim. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the core mathematical content right: it has the correct ambient dimension (4-manifold), the correct starting datum (a foliation by surfaces, hence an integrable rank-2 plane field), and the correct goal (perturbing toward an Engel structure). This matches the official problem stated in Question 2.16 of §2.5. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question stand-alone, it helps to say explicitly that the foliation is a rank-2 integrable subbundle Tℱ ⊂ TM, since Engel structures are also rank-2 plane fields and the perturbation is really of Tℱ. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper immediately adds a hidden necessary topological condition: because an Engel structure splits TM into line bundles, one must assume that Tℱ and a complementary rank-2 bundle split as direct sums of line bundles. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The notion of Engel structure should be spelled out for completeness: in §2.5 it is defined as a rank-2 distribution D on a 4-manifold such that E := [D,D] is a hyperplane field and E is even-contact, i.e. [E,E] = TM. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper does not impose extra hypotheses such as closedness, compactness, orientability, or coorientability in Question 2.16, so those should not be added in the refined version. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper leaves the topology of the perturbation implicit; if one wants a sharper stand-alone question, one should phrase it as perturbing or approximating Tℱ among smooth rank-2 plane fields. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a smooth 4-manifold equipped with a foliation ℱ by surfaces, so that Tℱ ⊂ TM is an integrable rank-2 distribution. Assuming the necessary splitting condition noted in the paper—namely that Tℱ and a complementary rank-2 subbundle of TM both split as direct sums of line bundles—can the tangent plane field Tℱ be perturbed, among smooth rank-2 plane fields on M, to an Engel distribution D ⊂ TM (that is, a rank-2 distribution for which E := [D,D] is a rank-3 even-contact hyperplane field and [E,E] = TM)? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: This paper is a problem list, and the draft clearly targets the Engel subsection rather than any Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3. The closest official formulation is Question 2.16 in §2.5, which the draft nearly reproduces word for word. The nearby context at the start of §2.5 supplies the definition of Engel structure, and the sentence immediately after Question 2.16 supplies the key hidden assumption about splitting into line bundles. Question 2.17 is a separate codimension-1, leafwise-contact variant; it is not stated as equivalent, so the refined question should stay with Question 2.16 and only incorporate the explicit splitting caveat. Also, there are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency parameters in this problem; it is purely a differential-topological question about rank-2 distributions on 4-manifolds. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
